ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a mountain area elevation relationship graph, with the horizontal axis as Altitude (m), the left vertical axis as Average temperature (°C), and the right vertical axis as Abundance (Number per km²). The blue curve indicates the change of average temperature with altitude; the black abundance curves are respectively labeled as Species 1, Species 2, and Species 3. The black curve of Species 1 appears in the lower-altitude region and already has abundance greater than zero below 500 m; the curve of Species 2 begins only around approximately 600 m; the curve of Species 3 appears only at higher altitudes. Reasoning: The question asks which tree species are at altitudes below 500 m. Looking only at the left side of 500 m on the horizontal axis, only the abundance curve of Species 1 is greater than zero, and Species 2 and Species 3 have not yet appeared. Therefore, the tree species below 500 m is Species 1 only.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it is a mountain altitude graph with black abundance curves for three species and a 500 m mark on the x-axis. Then examine only the portion of the graph left of 500 m. The Species 1 curve is present above zero in this region, while Species 2 begins only above about 600 m and Species 3 begins much higher. Therefore the species found below 500 m is Species 1 only.
